subject.title: [Bug] sessions_yield on a required-completion spawned run finalizes the task as blocked ("Required completion did not produce a final deliverable") at first turn end; the real final reply never announces

question: Should maintainers require a live current-main reproduction before allowing a narrow fix for required-completion `sessions_yield` finalization, or is the source-backed failure shape sufficient to proceed?
rationale: The source path explains the exact blocked terminal summary, but the reporter's key claim is that live metadata is lost or races despite existing `yielded: true` guards, and this review did not prove that loss site on current main.

options.title: Require live repro first
options.body: Run a packaged gateway or Crabbox scenario that spawns a required-completion subagent, yields on turn one, resumes, and checks whether the task finalized early before choosing the fix boundary.

options.title: Proceed with narrow hardening
options.body: Treat the source-backed failure shape as enough to patch the required-completion lifecycle path, while adding a focused regression for missing or late yield marker handling.

options.title: Fold into broader delivery work
options.body: Track this under the broader subagent completion-loss umbrella and avoid a separate fix until the durable delivery policy is chosen.

recommendation.title: Require live repro first
recommendation.body: Run a packaged gateway or Crabbox scenario that spawns a required-completion subagent, yields on turn one, resumes, and checks whether the task finalized early before choosing the fix boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The current split registry/finalization files and recent area history point to this owner as the closest routing candidate for deciding proof sufficiency on the implicated paths.
